questions.q: What does SERVERPROPERTY('Edition') return, and why does it matter to a DBA?
options: The SQL Server edition (Standard, Enterprise, Developer, etc.), which matters because features like Online Index Rebuild differ by edition
The current database's recovery model
The number of databases currently on the instance
The list of logins with sysadmin rights
questions.explain: Edition determines which engine features are available — Enterprise-only features like certain online operations won't work on Standard.

questions.q: Which function would you use to check whether a specific database is set to SIMPLE or FULL recovery model?
options: DATABASEPROPERTYEX('DbName', 'Recovery Model')
SERVERPROPERTY('RecoveryModel')
sys.dm_exec_requests
OBJECT_ID('DbName')
questions.explain: DATABASEPROPERTYEX() takes a database name and property name and returns database-level settings like recovery model.

questions.q: Why are IsAutoClose and IsAutoShrink flagged as common 'why is this database slow' culprits?
options: Auto-close tears down and reopens the database on every idle period, and auto-shrink fights constantly with growth, fragmenting the database
They disable all indexes automatically
They prevent backups from ever completing
They are only relevant to tempdb, never to user databases
questions.explain: Auto-close adds overhead reopening the database repeatedly, and auto-shrink causes ongoing fragmentation as the file shrinks and regrows.

questions.q: What does SERVERPROPERTY('ProductVersion') tell a DBA that's useful during an incident?
options: The exact build number, useful for checking whether a known bug or fix applies to this instance
The name of the currently logged-in user
The total memory allocated to the buffer pool
The list of all databases on the instance
questions.explain: ProductVersion (paired with ProductLevel) identifies the exact patch level, which is often the first thing checked when a known issue might be in play.

questions.q: For scanning recovery model and auto-close settings across every database on an instance at once, which approach is typically faster?
options: Querying sys.databases directly, rather than calling DATABASEPROPERTYEX() once per database
Restarting the SQL Server service and reading the startup log
Calling SERVERPROPERTY() once per database
There is no way to check more than one database at a time
questions.explain: sys.databases returns recovery_model_desc, is_auto_close_on, and similar columns for every database in one query, which is more efficient than calling DATABASEPROPERTYEX() per database.
